repo: gsd-tools commit helper has a known false-negative: it can report `commit_failed` even though the commit landed cleanly — always verify with `git log` before treating it as a real failure.

The `plan:pre` UI capability hook only fires when the registry's `when` condition classifies the phase as net-new UI surface; architecture/refactor phases like 68.2 correctly get zero UI hooks even though the lower-level `ui-plan-gate` check reports `block:true`.
Nyquist validation requires a `## Validation Architecture` section in RESEARCH.md to populate VALIDATION.md.

`worktree.baseRef: "head"` means parallel executor worktrees fork from live HEAD (carrying all in-progress planning commits), not from `origin/main` — must be checked before dispatching worktree executors or they'll miss PLAN.md files.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree executors each need their own `pnpm install`, which is expensive per worktree — for waves that are mostly single-plan, sequential execution on the main tree is more efficient and equally correct when same-wave plans are file-disjoint.
Web executors must rebuild the SDK dist before web typecheck after any cross-package SDK change, otherwise typecheck runs against a stale dist (cross-package staleness landmine).

REQUIREMENTS.md checkboxes for requirements spanning multiple plans (e.g. SDK-READ-01/02/04) must not be marked `[x]` until every constituent plan (including the deletion plan) lands — early executors mistakenly self-marked them complete after only the addition half was done.

Deleting shared modules (kind-cache, useFileSize, ipns.service.ts, file-metadata.service.ts) requires mapping ALL importers first — the actual blocking surface (~15+ importers including fileTypes.ts, key-wrapping.ts, vault-settings.store.ts, TextEditorDialog.tsx, useStreamingPreview.ts) was significantly wider than the plan initially scoped.

`resolveChildren`'s per-child graceful-skip-on-failure design is security-sound because the target folder is already gated via `ensureFolderLoaded`/`dfsFindFolder` before it runs — an unverifiable sibling is simply omitted rather than rendered with stale/attacker content.

code.finding: New ROT-07 `enforceResolved` gate added on the SDK-internal read path at root resolve.
New ROT-07 `enforceResolved` gate added at the `dfsFindFolder` child loop, alongside the pre-existing write-path gate at line 1156.

Docstring explains why `resolveChildren`'s per-child skip-on-failure is safe: the folder is gated before this runs, so omission (not stale render) is the failure mode, and navigating into any child re-triggers the gate.

workflow: For security-critical or deviation-flagged plan output, independently re-run acceptance tests rather than trusting the executor's self-reported PASS — this caught nothing wrong here but is the correct discipline.

ScheduleWakeup delay must be computed from the actual current time at the moment of scheduling, not an earlier cached timestamp — a quota interruption between computing and calling caused a ~25min drift (04:35 instead of 4:10am), requiring a second corrective call.
A pending ScheduleWakeup that can't be cleanly retracted is not fatal if the agent's session context persists across it — it just fires as a no-op once the awaited work is already done.
Use plain `git worktree add` (not a tool that migrates the current session) when the goal is to keep driving work in the current checkout while a second, independent workstream runs elsewhere.

AskUserQuestion is appropriate for genuine architectural/scope decision gates (research-vs-skip, D-07 boundary scope) but not for routine gate results — routing decisions with clear precedent should proceed without prompting.
